pr.title: BUG: Test the rank of the IV inputs after scaling the columns
pr.body:
Addresses case 3 of #823.

The rank checks in `_validate_inputs` call `matrix_rank` on the raw regressor and instrument matrices. `matrix_rank` thresholds the singular values relative to the largest one, so columns on very different scales look rank deficient even when they are not:

```python
z = rng.standard_normal((500, 2))
x = z @ [1.0, 1.0] + rng.standard_normal(500)
y = 1 + 0.5 * x + rng.standard_normal(500)

IV2SLS(y, np.ones((500, 1)), x, z * [1.0, 1e13]).fit()
# ValueError: instruments [exog instruments]  do not have full column rank
```

## Change

Both rank checks now scale the columns to unit length first, so the result does not depend on the units of the variables. A column that is exactly 0 cannot be scaled and is still detected as linearly dependent.

This is only the third case of #823; the LIML kappa cases (1 and 2) are untouched, since they need the relative-residual test and the joint change to the scaling of kappa.

## Tests

- Added `test_instr_rank_check_is_scale_invariant` in `tests/iv/test_model.py`; it fits the model with an instrument scaled by `1e13` and compares the estimates with the unscaled ones.
- `linearmodels/tests/iv/`: 9522 passed, 2400 skipped.
- `ruff check` and `numpydoc lint` pass on the changed files.

discussion.body: Gentle ping on this one — CI is green (15/15) and it is a small, self-contained bug fix. Would appreciate a review when you get a chance. Thanks!

I'm not a fan of this.  the regression is in the scale of the original columns, and if they are poorly scaled the numerics of the regression may be problematic.  A rank check in the same scale as the regression should help protect the user from these numeric problems. What do you think?

We need these permissions to access your repositories in order to provide you with the best experience possible. We will be setting up commit hooks to analyze every commit and pull request faster. Don’t worry, we don’t modify any of your code!

[Learn more about the required permissions](https://docs.codacy.com/getting-started/which-permissions-does-codacy-need-from-my-account/#github-cloud)

limitations: GraphQL returned HTTP 401; REST API used instead.
